thumbnail_brief: One huge northern giant hornet, mandibles open, over a pile of whole round cartoon bees with X eyes, tiny Doug in a bee costume (red cap on top) at the edge of the pile, with the words ONE BY ONE, so the title gives the numbers (30 hornets, 30,000 bees, an afternoon) and the thumbnail shows how it happens (no HORNETS, BEES, 30 or 30,000 on the image; no blood, no bee heads or body parts, no smiling bees). Variant B: Doug in the bee costume, arms folded at the hive entrance, one hornet landing beside him and a line of hornets arriving, IT BRINGS FRIENDS. Variant C: a hornet carrying a round brown bundle (no parts visible) home to a row of open-mouthed hornet larvae, BABY FOOD.
description:
A few dozen northern giant hornets, the largest hornets in the world, can wipe out a honeybee colony of 30,000 in about three hours, then carry the hive's young home as baby food. Doug follows the giant hornet from one bee to one hive to one person to one continent, ending in a tree in Washington State in 2020 that could have produced nearly 200 hornet queens.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe and watch Doug's death counter keep climbing.
